title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: manage workforce requests from Microsoft 365 Copilot chat
summary: Hold: the briefing says Microsoft documents no way to disable just the workforce request tools, but Service Agent documents organization-level visibility controls for individual MCP tools. The role-assignment path and API are supported, and the roadmap dates and availability match.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes WEM integration with Microsoft 365 Copilot through MCP tools.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 Workforce Engagement Management (WEM) integrates with Microsoft 365 Copilot through Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools.

claims.where: front matter: products; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The listed products are Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365) and Dynamics 365 Customer Service.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Dynamics 365 Customer Service"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target date is July CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "July CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) is the only cloud listed in the roadmap record.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists the Web platform.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: WEM offers three MCP tools for listing requests, opening request details and deciding time-off requests.
claims.quote: `list_wem_requests` | List workforce requests; `get_wem_request_details` | Get request details; `decide_wem_time_off_request` | Approve or reject time-off requests

claims.claim: Representatives and supervisors do not typically use the MCP tools directly.
claims.quote: Customer service representatives and supervisors don't typically use MCP tools directly. Instead, they interact with Service Agent.

claims.claim: Service Agent selects and invokes the tool in the background and presents the result in conversation.
claims.quote: Service Agent determines which tool to use, invokes it in the background, and presents the result in the conversation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The Learn overview names Service Agent as an example conversational experience.
claims.quote: These tools connect a conversational experience, such as Service Agent, with Dynamics 365 Customer Service and Dataverse

claims.claim: Request lists appear as an interactive list inside chat.

claims.claim: The time-off decision tool is named decide_wem_time_off_request.

claims.quote: It never overwrites a decision another reviewer already made

claims.claim: Representatives can check the status of their requests.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; changes
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for the new WEM request tools.
claims.quote: Searched: WEM tools default enabled; WEM request MCP tools default enabled Service Agent. Read WEM overview, all three tool pages, configure-service-agent and Service Agent FAQ excerpts; host setup is documented, but the new WEM tools' arrival default is not.
claims.fix: Keep defaultState unknown, but replace the broad sentence in Why it matters with 'Microsoft has not stated the arrival default for these WEM tools. Service Agent itself requires administrator configuration.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/customer-service/use/service-agent-faq for the second sentence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No licence entitlement specific to these WEM request tools is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Workforce Engagement Management MCP tools licensing license pricing; "Workforce Engagement Management" "MCP" "license". Read WEM overview, tool pages, WEM app prerequisites and Service app requirements; no WEM-tool-specific licence was named.
claims.fix: The product-level licence is published. Set licensing.model to included and add to its notes: 'Microsoft Copilot is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on for eligible subscription plans. Licensing specific to these WEM tools is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-license-options. Do not assert that additional tool charges are ruled out.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The WEM overview and tool pages name no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: WEM MCP tools licensing license. Read the complete WEM overview and list_wem_requests, get_wem_request_details and decide_wem_time_off_request pages; none names a licence.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no meter or charge specific to these WEM tools.
claims.quote: Searched: Workforce Engagement Management MCP tools pricing; Workforce Engagement Management licensing price. Read WEM overview, three tool pages, Service app requirements and Copilot licensing excerpts; none gives a WEM-tool-specific meter or charge.

claims.claim: The roadmap record does not identify which licence covers the tools.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)", "Dynamics 365 Customer Service"]

claims.claim: list_wem_requests defaults to team scope.
claims.quote: `scope` | `self` or `team`. **Defaults to `team`**—everything you can access.

claims.claim: Without a request-type filter the list includes every request type the caller can access.
claims.quote: When `requestType` is omitted, the tool returns **all** request types (time-off, shift-swap, shift-bid)

claims.claim: With no date filters, listing applies no date restriction.
claims.quote: When neither `from` nor `to` is supplied, the tool applies no date filter (all dates)

claims.claim: With no status filter the list spans all statuses.
claims.quote: By default, it shows all requests you can access, of **every type**, across all dates and statuses.

claims.claim: The default result limit is 25.
claims.quote: `top` | Integer maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 200.

claims.claim: The result limit is capped at 200.
claims.quote: `top` | Integer maximum number of requests to return. Defaults to 25, capped at 200.

claims.claim: Team-scope listing relies on Dataverse and WEM security.
claims.quote: for the default `scope: team`, it relies on Dataverse and WEM security to return only rows the caller can read.

claims.claim: Time-off request details can include notes.
claims.quote: **Time-off requests**—time-off type, whether it's a full day, the start and end of the time off, hours, and notes.

claims.claim: Shift-bid and shift-swap details can include review information.
claims.quote: **Shift-bid requests**—the request's status, dates, and review information. **Shift-swap requests**—the request's status, dates, and review information.

claims.claim: Time-off details include the time-off window.
claims.quote: Review the request's details, matched to its type—the time-off window for a time-off request

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; summary; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Dynamics 365 and Dataverse security limit tool responses and actions to the signed-in user's authorised access.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 and Dataverse security govern access to WEM MCP tools. Tool responses are limited to the records and actions the signed-in user is authorized to access.

claims.quote: Searched: Dynamics 365 Workforce Engagement Management MCP reviewer permission security role msdyn_wemrequest time off. Read WEM overview, decision reference and WEM roles page; reviewer access is required but no MCP-to-WFM-role mapping is stated.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and api; controls[1].note; Governance controls final paragraph
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no control that turns off only the WEM request tools.
claims.quote: Use this capability when you want to hide or show MCP tools at the organization or profile level. Maker tools cannot be hidden.
claims.fix: Remove the both-null controls[1] row and the repeated no-setting assertion. Replace that assertion with 'Service Agent supports organization- and profile-level visibility overrides for individual MCP tools; a profile can restore a tool hidden at organization level.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/developer/reference/mcp-tools/save_tool_selection and https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/configure-service-agent-experiences. Do not describe visibility overrides as an unoverrideable tenant-wide enforcement switch.

claims.claim: Service app deployment is managed at the app level.

claims.fix: Remove the first Before rollout checklist bullet, which asks readers to take stock of WEM enablement and package installation without corresponding control rows. Keep the prerequisites already stated in Scope; do not add rows.
